findings.title: Before adoption, LaunchServices launcher termination is classified as host termination
evidence: native_cause.py:49-57 constructs LaunchServices HostProcess, checks poll before verify_session, with no earlier adoption.
test-runtime.py:99 initializes pid=None; 115 launches /usr/bin/open; 199-200 returns open.poll when pid is None.
findings.conclusion: The failing cause-host-exited guard observed a non-None launcher status. It does not establish spontaneous browser exit. Launcher exact exit code was not preserved.
findings.minimalRepair: Shared harness poll should attempt existing passive exact-argv discovery and report an unobserved browser as unknown, without converting any launcher exit status into browser death. Keep bounded startup waits and mandatory verify_session unchanged.

findings.title: Do not rebind adopted identity while retaining an earlier kernel monitor
evidence: _adopt:155 replaces identity/PID unconditionally; 156-165 registers only when exit_events is None.
findings.minimalRepair: Reject a different PID/birth/argv identity after adoption, while making identical adoption idempotent. Preserve the existing kernel monitor and verify_session profile/PID/exact-argv checks.

findings.title: Preserve pre-cleanup ownership and launcher/browser statuses through the suite report
evidence: native_cause.py:120-141 records cleanupComplete but has no pre-cleanup host snapshot; poll at 122/137 is outside independent error capture.
native_suite.py:94-96 projects only seven cause fields.
findings.minimalRepair: Capture a bounded allowlist before cleanup, including launcher code and distinct identityObserved/verified/liveness/browser-code/requested-signal fields. Guard snapshot, cleanup and result saving independently, retain the first failure, and project those safe fields into native-summary.

findings.title: Post-cleanup disappearance is not proof of spontaneous browser exit
evidence: test-runtime.py:247-250 may passively discover an unconnected browser and then terminate it.
Outer nativeCleanup signalsToVerifiedOwnedInstances counts its own registry cleanup, not HostProcess.close signaling.
findings.minimalRepair: Keep before/after cleanup separate and mark unobserved identity/liveness as unknown. Do not infer crash, security rejection or authentication failure from cleanupComplete/allOwnedGone.
